steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What number should be passed to each callScene function so that the user is taken to the scene that matches their response?


Solution:

callScene function calls should be added inside the else if conditions for scenes 1, 2, and 5 in the callScene function definition. The argument passed should match the scene number of the user’s response in the question arrays.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which parameters should be updated in the printDialog functions so that the dialog text is fully visible in each scene?


Solution:

The x, y, and/or background parameters in the printDialog functions in scenes 3 and 4 of the callScene function definition should be updated so that the text appears fully on screen. The text should not block the rest of the background image. A background color should be added, as needed, to create a clear contrast against the background image.


Ask the ninja: 

❓  What should be changed in the endScreenText image asset so that the user knows the project has ended?


Solution:

The text drawn to the canvas in the endScreenImage image asset should be changed from “A Cat’s Day” to “The End”.
steps.instructions:
Fix the bugs in the code and the paint editor to create a working project!


Whenever a menu appears on screen, the user should be taken to the scene that matches their response after they select an option.


Whenever dialog text appears on screen, it should be fully visible (not cut off) and have a clear contrast against the background image.


In the final scene, the text in the background image should tell the user that they’ve reached the end of the project.


Use the functions in the code menu and the paint editor tools to create a working version of this project!

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 9 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about adding User Interface (UI) features, such as splash and game over screens, user choice, and game narrative that can significantly improve the User Experience (UX) of a project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 9:

badges.title: Screen Time
badges.description: Use a variety of pixel art techniques to create full-screen image assets to enhance the user experience in a project.

badges.title: An Asset for Every Season
badges.description: Create 160x120 full-screen image assets that can be layered on top of one another to create a variety of game screens.

badges.title: Flavor Text
badges.description: Use the Text Sprite extension to create custom scene titles, directions, and variable counters on screen.

badges.title: Choose Your Adventure
badges.description: Create a personalized experience for the user by changing scenes based on their responses.

badges.title: Reliable Narrator
badges.description: Use the Story extension to create narrative scenes that describe what’s happening in the project.

badges.title: Chain of Command
badges.description: Convert a number value to a string.

badges.title: Red Light Green Light
badges.description: Pause a project until any button is pressed to make screens remain as long as a user chooses.
